question: How much should an Experiments switch say under its name?
context: The Experiments window lists every feature switch with a description. 92 of 95 run over 40 words (median 179, longest 557). A test now stops any of them growing; this decides how short the rewrite makes them.

options.label: One sentence, about 25 words
options.summary: Each switch says what it changes in one plain sentence, like 'Adds the release name to editor window titles.' Nothing more in the window.
pros: Reads at a glance down a long list
Forces the point to the front
cons: No room to say what Off means
options.mitigation: Off is only spelled out where the switch's name leaves it unclear, as a second clause.

options.label: Two short sentences, up to 40 words
options.summary: What the switch changes, then what Off means. For example: 'The toast after a capture shows an Edit button and its key. Off means Edit only appears while the pointer is over the toast.'
pros: Says both sides of the switch
Matches the 40 words the budget was first filed with
cons: A list of 95 two-sentence descriptions is still a lot to scan
options.mitigation: The window's search still finds a switch by any word in it.

options.label: Leave them as they are
options.summary: Descriptions keep their full detail, up to 557 words. The test still stops any from growing and any new switch from going over 40.
pros: Every detail stays in the window
cons: Median description is 179 words; nobody reads them
